scope: Interpreter artifact, named library versions, enforced env_lock values, and only the two extension modules explicitly fingerprinted by run_path._environment. No installed-library or dyld sweep.

library_version_enforcement.py_ecc: run_path._environment compares the recorded py_ecc_version with the imported package version; mismatch refuses naming the module path and runtime register. The independent py_ecc 8.0.0 requirement is retained.
library_version_enforcement.numpy: run_path._environment compares the recorded numpy_version with the imported package version; mismatch refuses naming the module path and runtime register.
library_version_enforcement.astropy: run_path._environment compares the recorded astropy_version with the imported package version; mismatch refuses naming the module path and runtime register.

invocation_enforcement: run_path._environment enforces the complete recorded invocation, exact executable and PYTHONPATH, literal PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, sys.dont_write_bytecode and all five thread settings. Python version and every env_lock_enforced_values field are compared independently of the scientific lock.

non_enforced_env_lock_fields.scope: E2 claims the same-process double evaluation that score_config performs, in this locked environment; the driver sets the thread variables above before importing numpy and records them; no cross-process bit-exactness is claimed

guarantees: Rehashing files can detect changes to the named on-disk interpreter and the two named NumPy extension artifacts.
Comparing the recorded versions and lock values can detect drift in those reported values. Every enforced env_lock value matched in the offline observation.

The consumer enforces this bounded runtime contract at stage entry and before stage record completion. The register remains authoring evidence; no environment installation, adoption or actual study run is established.
limits: TOCTOU: extension modules are hashed by read_pin and later imported by Python with no lock between. These pins evidence what was on disk at check time, not what the loader used or what is already loaded. The consumer re-verifies both named extension digests immediately before the NumPy imports; this narrows the interval but does not remove it or attest loaded bytes.
Version strings do not identify every package byte or transitive dependency. No byte-level identity is claimed for py_ecc, astropy, NumPy Python sources or their full dependency trees.

Interpreter digest follows the invocation path's symlink to the resolved executable. It does not cover the Python framework, standard library, loader, shared libraries, OS, TLS trust store or in-memory relocated code.

Only the NumPy core and FFT extensions have explicit file pins and loaded-module path checks. Dynamically resolved Astropy, cytoolz and other extensions, their shared-library dependencies and dyld-resolved images remain outside this bounded byte pin; package versions are not binary identity.

Disabled bytecode writing does not disable reading existing .pyc files. CORE verifies all recorded local-code caches, requires an entry for each currently discoverable standard cache of its local source aliases, and compares cached code objects against compiled pinned source. Third-party caches and custom import loaders remain outside this bounded pin.
No cross-process or cross-machine bit-exactness, complete dependency closure, scientific correctness, authorization or successful study run is guaranteed.

current_driver_compatibility.reason: V46 run_path consumes A1-RUNTIME-PINS-CORE-1, verifies every recorded artifact and alias, checks the loaded paths of the two named NumPy extensions, all four Python/library versions and both representations of the scientific lock. Generic loaded-site-packages coverage is no longer required under the two-register decision.
